t: Will AI Transform Teaching and Learning? November 22, 2024
q: Over the past century, every technology introduced to improve teaching and learning has been hyped as “revolutionary” and ”transformational.
Yet there is little evidence that classroom use of these previous technologies forced classroom teachers to rethink, much less reshape, their instruction.
So I have concluded that those pushing AI use in classrooms fail to understand the complexity of teaching.
Anyone who has taught at least three to five years appreciates the extensive knowledge, skills, and emotional connections needed to get kindergartners, fifth graders, or high school seniors to learn.
Teaching, then, is not a mechanical act of connecting dots. Teaching is a complex act that requires knowledge of subject matter, managerial skills, and emotional labor.
While I believe AI will not force practitioners to rethink how they teach, nonetheless, as so many teachers have done in the past, they will adapt AI to fit the contours of their classrooms.
Or maybe AI in classrooms will become just a footnote in a future doctoral student's dissertation. Too early to say.

t: Designing the Perfect Assessment System, Part 1
q: One of the major challenges of designing a good assessment system is that there are a lot of important and competing purposes of assessment.

An assessment that would be perfectly designed for one purpose will not work well for another. Trying to make one assessment fit lots of purposes generally means it ends up fulfilling none of the purposes.
GCSEs were essentially designed to fulfil purpose 1 above. Over time, teachers ended up using them to give feedback and shape the curriculum, the government started using them to judge schools.
This led to lots more students getting the C grade, but the C grade stopped meaning what it had meant previously.
A feature of all these tests is that they are completely decoupled from school accountability and individual attainment.
As soon as 2011, surveys showed that schools had stopped teaching science as much and had reallocated the time to English and maths, which were still being tested.
So the samples have been good at identifying a problem, but can’t provide much information that would help fix it.
